{{short description|Tibetic language}} {{Infobox language | name = Gyalsumdo | altname = | nativename = {{lang|gyo|ग्याल्सुस्दो}} | states = [[Nepal]] | speakers = 200 | date = 2011 | ref =e25 | familycolor = Sino-Tibetan | fam1 = [[Sino-Tibetan]] | fam2 = [[Tibeto-Burman]] | fam3 = [[Tibeto-Kanauri]] | fam4 = [[Bodish]] | fam5 = [[Kyirong–Kagate languages|Kyirong–Kagate]] | dia1 = | dia2 = | dia3 = | dia4 = | script = | iso3 = gyo | glotto=gyal1236 }} '''Gyalsumdo''' ({{lang|gyo|ग्याल्सुस्दो}}) is a mostly undocumented [[Tibetic languages|Tibetic language]] spoken by an estimated 200 individuals of the [[Manang District, Nepal|Manang District]] in the [[Gandaki Zone]] of [[Nepal]].{{Cite web|url=http://languagelandscape.org/language/Gyalsumdo|title=Language Landscape|website=languagelandscape.org|access-date=2019-01-11}}{{Cite web|url=https://elar.soas.ac.uk/Collection/MPI1031990|title=Preliminary documentation and description of Gyalsumdo, an undocumented Tibetan language of Manang, Nepal|website=Endangered Languages Archive at SOAS University of London}} In January 2018 the language was added to [[ISO 639-3]] under the code "gyo."{{Cite web|url=https://iso639-3.sil.org/code/gyo|title=gyo {{!}} ISO 639-3|website=iso639-3.sil.org|access-date=2019-01-11}} Gyalsumdo is a [[Tone (linguistics)|tonal language]]; however in Gyalsumdo, unlike most other [[Tibetic languages|Central Tibetan]] languages, the word, rather than the syllable acts as the [[Tone (linguistics)|tone bearing unit]]. The language is reportedly closely related to the nearby [[Nubri language|Nubri]] and [[Tsum language|Tsum]] languages which share a large proportion of vocabulary. Gyalsumdo is also described as being somewhat [[Mutual intelligibility|intelligible]] by speakers of [[Nar Phu language|Nar-Phu]].{{Cite journal|last=Hildebrandt|first=Kristine|date=2015|title=A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Languages of Manang, Nepal: Co-Existence and Endangerment|url=https://www.academia.edu/10518392|journal=14|volume=Journal of Indigenous Nationalities}} ==Phonology== === Consonants === There are 30 consonants in Gyalsumdo, which are summarized in the table below. :{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" |- ! colspan="2" | !
